record.original_question: For n >= 2, describe the set of real numbers xi such that there are constants c_1(xi), c_2(xi) > 0 with uniform lower bounds for approximation by algebraic numbers of degree at most n, while infinitely many algebraic numbers of degree exactly n achieve the corresponding Dirichlet-type upper bound.

evidence.quote: Question 5.2 (Bugeaud). Let n ≥ 2. Denote by Жn the set of real numbers ξ with the following property: there exists c1 (ξ) > 0 and c2 (ξ) > 0 such that for algebraic number α of degree ≤ n, |ξ − α| ≥ c2 (ξ)H(α)−n−1 , and such that there are infinitely many algebraic numbers α of degree exactly n with |ξ − α| ≤ c1 (ξ)H(α)−n−1 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an algebraic number $\alpha$, let $H(\alpha)$ denote its naive height (the maximum of the absolute values of the coefficients of its minimal polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ with coprime coefficients). Fix an integer $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{X}_n$ denote the set of real numbers $\xi$ with the following two properties:

(i) There exists a constant $c_2(\xi) > 0$ such that, for every algebraic number $\alpha$ of degree at most $n$,
$$|\xi - \alpha| \geq c_2(\xi)\, H(\alpha)^{-n-1};$$

(ii) There exist a constant $c_1(\xi) > 0$ and infinitely many algebraic numbers $\alpha$ of degree exactly $n$ such that
$$|\xi - \alpha| \leq c_1(\xi)\, H(\alpha)^{-n-1}.$$

Describe (in as explicit a manner as possible) the set $\mathcal{X}_n$: determine, for each $n \geq 2$, what real numbers $\xi$ belong to $\mathcal{X}_n$, and in particular whether $\mathcal{X}_n$ is non-empty, its measure-theoretic and Hausdorff-dimensional properties, and how it relates to standard classes of transcendental numbers.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct search did not locate a published resolution to this specific question of Bugeaud describing the set $\mathcal{X}_n$ of real numbers admitting simultaneous matching lower and upper bounds of order $H(\alpha)^{-n-1}$ for approximation by algebraic numbers of degree at most/exactly $n$. The general area (Wirsing's conjecture, exponents $w_n^*$) remains active with only partial results (e.g., recent improvements to lower bounds on $w_n^*(\xi)$), and no explicit description of this set appears in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Exponents of Diophantine approximation — Y. Bugeaud (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of exponents w_n, w_n^* and related questions in approximation by algebraic numbers of bounded degree.
status_evidence.claim: The area surrounding Wirsing's problem and the exponent n+1 for degree-n approximation is surveyed with many questions still open.

status_evidence.title: On approximation to a real number by algebraic numbers of bounded degree (arXiv:2405.08341)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results improving lower bounds for w_n^*(xi), still short of the conjectural value n.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress establishes only partial bounds, indicating the precise description of sets like X_n is not settled.
